subject: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: AWS Partner Ops <aws-partner-ops@amazon.com>, Azure Marketplace Team <eu-marketplace@azure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Sep 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing

Hi team,

Quick one — Nimble Analytics (prospect for co-sell) has drafted their marketplace listing copy and are calling out a "24/7 global support" claim that will appear in the EU marketplace pages. The draft and support evidence are attached.

Before we push this through the marketplace publication flow, we need two things clarified:

- Is "24/7 global support" acceptable in the EU listing copy if the seller operates a primary hub in CET with follow-the-sun handoffs via a 3rd-party MSP?
- Does the marketplace require explicit on-page hours per region (e.g., EU: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00 CET + emergency out-of-hours escalation) rather than a blanket 24/7 statement?

Marissa/Kim — can you review the attached support rotation PDF to see if it satisfies the evidence bar? If not, we should ask Nimble to amend the copy to something like "24/7 critical incident coverage with regionally staffed support hours" (open to better wording).

Elena — copying you so you're aware; if changes are needed Nimble may have to provide signed SOC evidence or a contract clause for the MSP.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbleanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Sep 2029 11:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the flag. A few clarifications from our side:

- Nimble runs its primary support center in Madrid (CET) staffed 08:00–20:00 local time Monday–Sunday.
- For nights and holidays we have an MSP (Globex Support) on a contractual rotation for critical incidents; MSP handles P1/P0 only and will escalate back to our engineers during CET daytime.
- We are prepared to provide the MSP contract excerpt and the SOC-lite report; attaching the support rotations PDF and logo usage PNG.

We prefer to keep "24/7 incident coverage" language because marketing says it's important for customers, but we're open to a footnote or parentheses that spells out hours by region if required.

Elena
Head of GTM, Nimble Analytics
elena@nimbleanalytics.com

Attachment: nimble_support_rotations.pdf
Attachment: logo_usage_guidelines.png

From: AWS Partner Ops <aws-partner-ops@amazon.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbleanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Sep 2029 14:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing

Hi all — thanks for the details. Quick guidance from AWS Marketplace policy team:

- "24/7" is permitted as long as the seller can substantiate the claim with operational evidence. Evidence can be: staffing schedules, MSP contract specifying coverage, or an on-call rotation matrix tied to monitored alerts.
- For EU listings, local language/regulatory concerns mean you should avoid implying onsite local coverage unless you have that. Saying "24/7 incident coverage (critical incidents handled by MSP during off-hours)" is acceptable.
- We recommend an on-page footnote (short) with an internal link to a detailed support matrix accessible from the listing.

If you can provide the MSP contract excerpt and the SOC-lite report, we can fast-track the copy review.

—AWS Partner Ops

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbleanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Sep 2029 09:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing

Thanks for the input, AWS — that guidance aligns with Redwood's marketplace playbook. Notes from my review of Nimble's attachments:

- The support rotation PDF outlines MSP handoffs but does not show a signed contract excerpt (only an SOW summary). We should request the MSP agreement clause that guarantees response times for P1/P0 and a named escalation contact.
- Logo usage PNG looks fine for marketplace badge, but we need a short brand clearance statement from Nimble confirming trademark ownership and permitted derivatives for EU locales.

Suggested next steps:
1) Elena: please attach (a) MSP contract excerpt, (b) SOC-lite or equivalent monitoring evidence, and (c) a one-paragraph brand clearance statement.
2) If Nimble prefers to keep marketing copy as "24/7 incident coverage," update the listing copy to the compromise phrasing AWS suggested and include a 1-sentence footnote that links to the support matrix.
3) Once received, I'll queue the dossier for Azure and AWS listing review — should be fast if docs are complete.

Kimberly — tagging you to confirm there are no EU-specific Marketplace iconography restrictions we should surface to Nimble.

Marissa
Director, Channel GTM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbleanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Sep 2029 16:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarify seller branding + support window claim for EU listing

Quick confirmation — no EU iconography blockers beyond the usual: avoid country flags next to support claims, and ensure trademark attributions for localized badges. Also confirm Nimble will include a single-line trademark attribution under the logo (we can provide exact copy).

If Nimble can send the MSP excerpt and the trademark statement today, we'll aim to publish after approvals from both AWS and Azure.

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park
Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
